items.title: Earl Foster Interview
items.q: Now I played with him too.

ctx.x: So he joined some other band out there, I guess. He did, he did. I think, though, this article I read about this pianist talked like Frankie Dooson went out there with him, wasn't it? Do you remember? There was a story about Frankie Dooson. There was one story. Yeah, Frankie Dooson went too, but he was a trombonist. Do you remember? Yeah.

Now I played with him too. Now sometime, I was able to play him. Oh, really? And I was playing with them people. You didn't think about it. That's right. I know he said it is that, but he was a rapper on Ballon Street, or a cemetery. I went to his house several times, and I called myself, I was a boy, you know. He used to come up, you know, he was a kind of bachelor, you know. Sometimes he'd go up there and fry eggs, you know. Yeah. Cooked living or the same thing he'd do. He used to play a job. He wasn't a…
I had trouble with Jack Carey with him. I learned a lot of time in the advertising and stuff. I never knew his brother.
